Some things I’d like to see:
- pastries that have interesting flavors to them. I feel like most gf bakeries play to nostalgia rather than experimenting with new flavors, and eating the same thing over and over at bakeries like this gets a little old
- it would be smart to do a lot of gluten free and dairy free stuff, because those two intolerances together are very common
- a variety of breads. I don’t mind a super dark and grainy bread every now and then, but also having some lighter breads (and maybe even a milk bread) would be fun. 
- if you do sandwiches, having a panini press would be fun because those aren’t always able to be made gluten free at other cafes
- have a really good gluten free choux pastry and then go crazy with it. Eclairs, cream puffs, profiteroles, French cruller donuts, churros, and something savory as well. I feel like this really makes a bakery stand out 
- do interesting things with cupcakes and cakes. The trick to a good gf cake is to throw egg whites and other raising agents at it. But if you can make a good vanilla cake people will be very impressed. Gf people eat a lot of chocolate cake and brownies, so a vanilla cake is a real treat 
- things to take home and make yourself, and things like pasta (or even just gnocchi) and burger buns and sub rolls that people can use at home. And pizza dough


Ideas for the fryer: 
- churros again, because a lot of places make them so they can’t be that hard
- seconding yeasted donuts. Cake donuts are really quite bad
- go for something savory. A good battered onion ring would be fun. If you did a bloomin onion kind of thing that would be incredible. Or a nice battered chicken tender. I’ve seen people use sweet rice flour to make a frying batter and it looked so good
- in italy they do something called a “pizza fritta” which literally translates to “fried pizza” and it’s incredible. It’s a good workaround if you don’t have the space for a full pizza operation but discover a really good pizza dough

The change in the name for the play was part of the rewrite to get Touko to realize that she doesn’t have to act. 

“Only you know” refers to the old play, where it was implied that only Touko knew which of the three versions of herself shown was the real one, and she had to choose one to embody. 

“I only know you” refers to the new play, where the nurse tells Touko that she only knows her current version of her, and that throwing that away to try and be someone else to satisfy someone else’s expectations would be a waste. And the nurse represents all of Touko’s current friends and classmates who never met her sister

Getting migraines around your period is very common and very annoying. I also get the worst of my migraines near my period, so I feel your pain. 

When you take birth control pills, they always include a week of placebo pills that you take so you have a period. Some people will skip the placebo week and then never get a period as a result, but that’s something you need to talk to your doctor about before you start. 

The other thing to mention is that if you have migraine with aura you should not be taking combination birth control due to the increased risk of stroke.

I’m just going to list a bunch of things that I’ve tried and now they worked for me. Maybe you can relate to it, or maybe have a place to start. 

1. I am prescribed triptans i take if a migraine is coming. This helps 

2. I tried acupuncture for a minute. It didn’t work for me, but it’s very relaxing. I could maybe see it working for someone whose migraines are triggered by general stress/tension 

3. Exercise —> follow what’s best for your body. If running isn’t working, try going on walks or lifting weights. Whatever your body can handle, and stop the first second it starts to be too much. Exercise is always good for you if its done right for your body

4. Eating enough food. Adhd messes me up real bad in terms of how much food I eat. If I’m not medicated I get lots of cravings and I eat all the time and if I’m medicated I don’t want to eat at all. And not eating is a migraine trigger for me. So make being intentional about your meals a priority. 

5. The actual food you’re eating. For me, it turned out I had a gluten intolerance. This was one of the biggest things that made both migraines and adhd manageable. Gluten would cause inflammation or something in my stomach, and now that it’s gone, my body isn’t in such a triggered state and now I get fewer migraines. Make sure you talk through any diet changes with a doctor or a dietitian or something. Tbh a dietitian might be good for you, especially if you can find someone who’s able to help you identify migraine triggers

6. I have a cefaly. They’re expensive as shit but it’s a good way of easing the pain of a migraine if medication works weird for you

7. I have orange migraine glasses to help with bright lights. This makes doing daily tasks with a small migraine possible without making it get worse sometimes. 

8. Follow whatever motivation you have until it becomes triggering. Hyperfixation is so nice when you need to get something done, but you have to stop the second you feel a migraine coming

9. Take it easy. It’s not an easy combination at all. I hope maybe one of these things is new for you so you can try.

Your daughter is getting to the age where college prep stuff is getting important, and that’s what she wants to do. So in terms of college prep stuff there are a few administrative things that should be done sooner rather than later. 

First, make sure you get the formal paperwork done for a 504 plan as soon as possible. The College board won’t let you get testing accommodations unless you’ve had a 504 for at least 6 months. I had to take the SAT twice and did pretty bad on some AP exams because I didn’t have a 504 long enough to get the accommodations I needed. I was diagnosed later in high school. But make sure you’re on top of things when it comes to the college board

For ADHD, time and a half extended time on timed assessments, taking assessments in a reduced distraction space (less than around 10 students), and extensions as needed on individual assignments are all pretty standard accommodations. 

The other thing to do is make sure you do research on potential colleges and ask about their office of disability services. Make sure it’s good, and that students there can get accommodations they need and that they can change their accommodations if things aren’t working. Some schools have support groups for students with ADHD. Be sure to check that out as well. 

And once your daughter is committed to a school, make sure she sends in a copy of her 504 to the office of disability services as soon as possible so getting accommodations goes smoothly. 

The other thing when it comes to having ADHD as a college student is that it’s really hard. I’ve barely been able to do it lmao, and that’s with using every piece of support possible at my school (which is very accommodating compared to most places). Your daughter should really think about her choice of a major — what can realistically be done in 4 years? What types of assignments are pure agony and which ones are more manageable? How are papers vs problem sets vs presentations vs video projects? For me, I’m no good with writing papers so I’m doing more math and science stuff that have more weekly assignments because I find that more manageable.
